t.7.88.1: Thus addressed by Vālmīki, Rāghava, with palms joined in reverence, replied in the midst of the world, having looked upon her who shone with the radiance of a goddess.
t.7.88.2: It is just as you say, O illustrious one, O knower of dharma; for through your stainless words, O brahman, I am convinced.
t.7.88.3: For long ago Vaidehī gave proof of her purity in the presence of the gods; yet, O brahman, though I knew she was sinless, I abandoned Sītā out of fear of the people, and so you should forgive me.
t.7.88.4: And I know that these twins, Kuśa and Lava, are my sons. Once Maithilī has been shown to be pure in the midst of the world, let my love be with her.
t.7.88.5: Then, having understood Rāma's intention, the foremost of the gods all assembled there, placing the Grandfather at their head.
t.7.88.6: The Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Viśvedevas, the hosts of the Maruts, the two Aśvins, the ṛṣis and Gandharvas, and likewise the troops of Apsarases, the Sādhyas, all those gods, and all the supreme ṛṣis as well.
t.7.88.7: Then Vāyu, best of the gods, auspicious and holy, divinely fragrant and delightful to the mind, gladdened that multitude of people on every side.
t.7.88.8: People from all the kingdoms, their minds intent, gaze upon that inconceivable thing as though it were a wonder, just as in the Kṛta age of old.
t.7.88.9: Seeing them all assembled, Sītā, clad in ochre robes, spoke these words with joined palms, her gaze cast down and her face lowered.
t.7.88.10: As I do not think of anyone other than Rāghava even in my mind, so may the goddess Mādhavī grant me an opening.
t.7.88.11: As Vaidehī was thus swearing her oath, there appeared that wondrous thing: a divine, unsurpassed lion-throne risen up from the surface of the earth.
t.7.88.12: It was borne upon the heads of those Nāgas of boundless might, divine, of heavenly form, and adorned with every kind of jewel.
t.7.88.13: And there the goddess Dharaṇī, taking Maithilī in her two arms, greeted her with a welcome and seated her upon a throne.
t.7.88.14: Seeing her seated upon the throne and entering Rasātala, an unbroken, heavenly shower of sacred flowers rained down upon Sītā.
t.7.88.15: And suddenly a very great cry of approval arose from the gods: "Well done, well done, O Sītā, you whose conduct is such as this!"
t.7.88.16: Thus the gods stationed in the sky, their hearts filled with joy, uttered words of many kinds as they beheld the entry of Sītā into the earth.
t.7.88.17: All those sages who had gathered at the sacrificial enclosure, and the kings too, tigers among men, could not cease from their astonishment.
t.7.88.18: In the sky and on the earth, all beings, both the unmoving and the moving, the huge-bodied Dānavas, and in Pātāla the lords of the serpents.
t.7.88.19: Some, thrilled with joy, cried out aloud; some were absorbed in contemplation; some gazed at Rāma, and some, as if senseless, gazed at Sītā.
t.7.88.20: Seeing Sītā's entry into the earth, they all came thronging together; for that moment the whole world was, as it were, utterly bewildered.
